summary: Aggregate native containment is not proven; reducing the allowance from 3GiB to 1.5GiB is not yet defensible. Existing evidence supports the fixed ext4 bound, manifest/mount/backing checks, selected path redirection, v2 input identity, persistent-config copying, and nonduplicated backing-image billing. However, telemetry has separate unredirected outputs, and the child retains write access outside the volume. These are engineering defects, distinct from pending production-volume provisioning, actual Kit dependency resolution, and CUDA/JIT compatibility. The noexec probe proves CPU LLVM behavior on tmpfs only. Reviewed source and existing test evidence; no tests or runtime operations executed. No runtime permission or scientific acceptance granted.
next_plan: Redirect telemetry outputs and enforce the child/descendant write boundary; add focused CPU escape-denial and output-routing tests, then independently review the repair. Keep 3GiB and capacity=false meanwhile. Before exact baseline admission, provision a fresh reserved volume, freeze source/v2 inputs and reconciled capacity, and bind exact Store authority. Authorized initialization must verify actual Kit resolution, native destinations and noexec compatibility with fail-closed cleanup. Do not extend the reduced allowance to training modes without equivalent enforcement.
must_fix: Uncontained telemetry writers: training_workloads/unified_h1/native_volume.py:settings and training_workloads/scale_003/resources.py redirect /log/file but omit /structuredLog/logDirectory and /telemetry/log/file. The frozen headless experience enables omni.kit.telemetry. Its reviewed KitTelemetry.md:200–218 explicitly states that the transmitter does not inherit /log/file and defaults to a separate log directory; its cloud file endpoint can also target ${omni_logs}. Explicitly bind the applicable structured-log/transmitter/file-endpoint destinations inside the native volume, preserve evidence, and test their launcher wiring/readback. Current job/attempt/native inventory does not discover these external outputs.

Missing aggregate write-boundary enforcement: training_workloads/unified_h1/local_dispatch.py:136–182 sets environment variables and execs with ordinary user filesystem access; training_workloads/unified_h1/extension_inputs.py validates hashes but does not make inputs read-only. The actual extension tree is mint-owned mode0775 and Kit data directory mint-owned mode0755. Neither settings readback nor PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE prevents native code or descendants from writing absolute paths outside the volume. Enforce a fail-closed write policy before execution, inherited by descendants, keeping runtime/assets/extensions read-only and permitting only the native volume plus explicitly bounded workload/control outputs. Add CPU counterexamples for outside-volume writes and input mutation. Until this exists, the ext4 limit and inventory's single-image billing cannot establish the proposed all-native 1.5GiB bound.
